children: chief executive Jensen Huang has agreed to answer lawmakers’ questions privately about his relationship with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, House China committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Sunday. A date has yet to be set for the appearance before members of three House committees.
For investors, the inquiry adds uncertainty about Nvidia’s
governance and its business in China. Findings could intensify scrutiny of the company’s efforts to influence U.S. chip-export restrictions, potentially affecting its access to a major market.
“That’s going to be a very important meeting to understand to what degree privileged information was accessed,” Moolenaar said on CBS’s
. Lawmakers also want to examine whether the relationship shaped Nvidia’s positions on export controls and artificial-intelligence policy.
Moolenaar said Huang’s voluntary cooperation removed the need for a subpoena. The congressional inquiry follows Huang’s departure from Nvidia
and appointed finance chief Colette Kress interim CEO.

title: Jensen Huang agrees to private congressional testimony on alleged China links
